access_links.label: Colosseum: The Open RAN Digital Twin (arXiv 2404.17317)

dedupe_keys.name: colosseum the open ran digital twin wireless network emulator

description: Colosseum is a large wireless network emulator with hardware in the loop, run by Northeastern University's Institute for the Wireless Internet of Things with funding from the US National Science Foundation and others, and generally available since 2 October 2020. It has 256 programmable software-defined radios and a radio-frequency channel emulator that can reproduce up to 65,536 channels of 100 MHz, so that researchers can run repeatable experiments on topologies representative of real cellular deployments. A 2024 tutorial paper describes it as an Open RAN digital twin: it combines the RF emulator with end-to-end O-RAN and 5G protocol stacks, tools to turn measured real-world RF environments into emulation scenarios (the CaST toolchain), automation pipelines for RF and protocol-stack twinning, and uses such as linking the twin to real networks and training and testing AI and machine-learning controllers. Academic, government and industry teams request access; the site reported 841 users in 165 teams in August 2026. Coverage: an emulation facility in the United States, usable remotely. Format and access: remote access over VPN after a team request, with a knowledge base, software images and training; free for approved research use. Caveats: access is by application and scheduling; scenarios are emulated, not field measurements. Simulation uses: digital twins of radio access networks for testing resilience, spectrum sharing and emergency configurations before deployment. Related records: NVIDIA Aerial Omniverse Digital Twin and ns-3 are simulation-based alternatives, and Sionna provides ray tracing.
